samf-senior-2020-r2-01.prompt: The sum of the digits of a 7-digit number is 6. What is the product of the digits?

samf-senior-2020-r2-02.prompt: How many of the first one hundred positive integers are divisible by all of the numbers 2, 3, 4 and 5?

samf-senior-2020-r2-03.prompt: Kerstin opens her dictionary and says: \"The sum of the number of the page I'm currently on and the number of the next page is 341\". On which page is Kerstin?

samf-senior-2020-r2-04.prompt: What is the smallest positive integer that you can multiply by 2020 to get a perfect square?

samf-senior-2020-r2-05.prompt: On four consecutive days David woke up at 5:30, 5:45, 7:30 and 7:55, respectively. On average, over the four days, how many minutes after 6:00 did he wake up?

samf-senior-2020-r2-06.prompt: One hundred students wrote the June examinations. Thirty students failed Physics, 25 failed Mathematics and 12 failed both subjects. How many students passed both subjects?

samf-senior-2020-r2-07.prompt: Consider the pyramid of numbers in the diagram. What is the second-to-last number in row six?

samf-senior-2020-r2-08.prompt: The graph describes a six-hour trip that Herman recently took. What was his average speed in km/h?

samf-senior-2020-r2-09.prompt: The difference between the square root and the fourth root of the same number is 12. What is the number?

samf-senior-2020-r2-10.prompt: If the repeating (recurring) decimal number $0.\dot 7$ is represented by the fraction $\frac ab$ in lowest terms, what is $a + b$?

samf-senior-2020-r2-11.prompt:
Andy has a number of red, green and blue counters. He places eight counters equally spaced around a circle according to the following rules:

- two red counters may not be placed next to each other,
- two green counters may not be placed diagonally opposite each other.

What is the smallest number of blue counters that Andy will need to use?

samf-senior-2020-r2-12.prompt: Each side of the large square is divided into three equal parts as shown in the figure. The area of the small shaded square is 9. What is the area of the large square?

samf-senior-2020-r2-13.prompt: Ellie spun a coin thirty times. Whenever the coin showed heads, Ellie gave two of her sweets to Pebetse. When the coin showed tails, Pebetse gave three of her sweets to Ellie. After 30 spins, both Ellie and Pebetse had the same number of sweets as they started with. How many times were heads spun?

samf-senior-2020-r2-14.prompt: None of the learners in a certain school know the rules of Sudoku. On 15 January a teacher teaches these rules to three learners. Every day after this, every learner who already learnt the rules, teaches them to two learners who do not know them yet. How many learners in the school know the rules of Sudoku by midnight on 20 January?

samf-senior-2020-r2-15.prompt: Square $ABCD$ has side length 60. Triangle $CDE$ and square $ABCD$ have equal areas. What is the distance of point $E$ to the extended line $AB$?

samf-senior-2020-r2-16.prompt: You have two friends, Odo and Priscilla. Everything Odo says on odd numbered days of the month is a lie while everything Priscilla says on prime numbered days of the month is a lie. On all other days they tell the truth. One day in January you meet these two friends sitting under a tree in the park. Priscilla says \"I have already lied on 13 days this month.\" Odo says \"I have lied on at least 13 days this month\", to which Priscilla responds, \"In fact, he has lied on less than 11 days this month\". Which day of the month is it?

samf-senior-2020-r2-17.prompt: If a quadrilateral $ABCD$ has an area of 60 and an inscribed circle with radius 3, what is the perimeter of quadrilateral $ABCD$?

samf-senior-2020-r2-18.prompt: At a certain university, 52 percent of all students pass; 48 percent of the male students pass and 55 percent of the female students pass. If the ratio of the number of male students who pass to the number of female students who pass is expressed as a fraction $\frac mf$ in lowest terms, determine $m + f$.

samf-senior-2020-r2-19.prompt: If $f(n + 1) = \dfrac{2f(n) + 1}{2}$ for every positive integer $n$, and $f(1) = 2$, determine $f(101)$.

samf-senior-2020-r2-20.prompt: Tom has 3 blue and 4 red balls in a bag. Dick takes 2 balls out of the bag and keeps them. Harry then takes out one of the balls left in the bag. If the probability of Harry taking out a blue ball is $\frac{x}{210}$, what is the value of $x$?

samf-senior-2020-r2-21.prompt: A supermarket has 128 crates of apples. Each crate contains at least 120 and at most 144 apples. What is the largest integer $n$ such that at least $n$ crates must contain the same number of apples?

samf-senior-2020-r2-23.prompt: How many triangles with positive areas in the $xy$-plane, and vertices with integer coordinates $(x; y)$, are there satisfying $1 \le x \le 4$ and $1 \le y \le 4$?

samf-senior-2020-r2-24.prompt: A circle $C$ has radius 5 and its centre is at $(-3; 2)$. Point $A$ has coordinates $(x; 2)$. $Q$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and traces out a circle as $B$ moves around the circumference of circle $C$. For what value of $x$ will the centre of the smaller circle formed by $Q$ lie on the circumference of circle $C$?

samf-senior-2020-r2-25.prompt: On level ground, a car travels at 63 km/h. Going uphill, it slows down to 56 km/h. Going downhill, it speeds up to 72 km/h. A trip from $A$ to $B$ by this car takes 4 hours. The return trip from $B$ to $A$ takes 4 hours and 40 minutes. What is the distance between $A$ and $B$?
